clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work and separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. Your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984, within the following months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free; and your own anxiety rose at bedtime, all in the same months. Your sister Ines was born in September 1984, and the shifts settled after.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, within the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news; they argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather developed chest pains; your father drank most evenings; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; and your parents fought over your father's evenings at his parents' house. Your grandmother moved to a nursing home in June 1997, and your father cut his drinking back by October, where the period settled.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's departure in May 1999 for a job up north, within the following months: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother's anxiety rose at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines everywhere with her; and Ines returned to school full days and passed her exams by August 2000, where the period settled.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following year: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going to the bookshop and were let go in May, dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark, and took a job at the garden centre by November where you slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
